nodes.content: Develop a learned plasma fluid closure that recovers collisionless plasma echoes while preserving energy under unseen forcing histories.
requirements: Predict echo amplitudes within 10% of Vlasov–Poisson reference values on held-out forcing histories.
Keep unforced total energy drift below 0.1% over 100 plasma periods.

nodes.content: Train a Hamiltonian moment closure with phase-resolved Fourier memory modes and energy-preserving triad couplings for plasma echoes.
How many phase-resolved memory modes capture echo rephasing across unseen pulse delays while maintaining Hamiltonian energy conservation?
Sixteen phase-resolved memory modes per wave number yield ≤10% echo-amplitude error on held-out delays and conserve semidiscrete energy.
Train 8-, 16-, and 32-mode closures on VP-Echo-1; compare held-out echo error, semidiscrete energy residual, and 100-period drift.
VP-Echo-1: 16 modes yielded 8.2% held-out echo error, 3×10⁻¹² semidiscrete energy residual, and 0.06% unforced 100-period drift.
Stress-test the 16-mode closure on VP-Echo-OOD's extrapolated pulse delays and three-pulse histories, measuring echo error and semidiscrete energy residual.
On VP-Echo-OOD extrapolated pulse delays, 16 modes produced 22% echo-amplitude error despite a 4×10⁻¹² semidiscrete energy residual.
Adaptive expansion from 16 to 32 modes at long delays will cut VP-Echo-OOD echo error below 10% while conserving energy.
Train zero-initialized 16-to-32-mode expansion at k v_th Δt>12; measure VP-Echo-OOD echo error, semidiscrete energy residual, and 100-period drift.
VP-Echo-OOD: adaptive 32-mode expansion reduced echo error from 22% to 8.6%, with 5×10⁻¹² semidiscrete energy residual and 0.07% 100-period drift.
Evaluate the adaptive closure on withheld three-pulse and chirped-amplitude histories, measuring peak echo error and 100-period unforced energy drift.
On VP-Echo-OOD long-delay three-pulse chirps, adaptive expansion yielded 17.4% peak echo error and 0.07% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Chirp-conditioned energy-preserving phase rotation of 32 modes should yield <10% three-pulse echo error and <0.1% 100-period unforced drift.
Fit chirp-conditioned skew-symmetric rotations for 16, 32, and 48 modes; compare held-out echo error and unforced energy drift.
Fit 16-, 32-, and 48-mode chirp-conditioned skew-symmetric rotations; measure VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse echo error and unforced 100-period energy drift.
VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse chirps: 32-mode phase rotation cut peak echo error from 17.4% to 8.7%; unforced 100-period energy drift was 0.08%.
Release EchoClosure-v1: 32-mode chirp-conditioned Hamiltonian closure, VP-Echo-OOD evaluation scripts, and reproducible 100-period energy-drift benchmarks.
Adopt chirp-conditioned 32-mode closure: adaptive modes solved delays (8.6%) but missed chirps (17.4%); phase rotation achieves 8.7% and 0.08% drift.
Train a reversible adaptive Hermite-moment closure with learned tail coupling and exact field-energy exchange to retain echo-producing filamentation.
Train 32- and 64-moment reversible Hermite closures; benchmark VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse chirp error and 100-period drift against EchoClosure-v1.
VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse chirps: 64-moment Hermite closure achieved 6.5% echo error and 0.04% 100-period drift versus EchoClosure-v1’s 8.7%/0.08%.
Release HermiteEcho-v1: 64-moment reversible closure, VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse evaluation scripts, and unforced 100-period energy-drift diagnostics.
Select HermiteEcho-v1 for three-pulse chirps: 6.5% echo error and 0.04% energy drift outperform EchoClosure-v1’s 8.7% and 0.08%.
Learn a causal Volterra-kernel closure with antisymmetric memory coupling, retaining forcing-history phase information while conserving fluid–field energy.
What Volterra memory horizon keeps held-out three-pulse echo error below 10% while preserving antisymmetric fluid–field energy exchange?
A 24-plasma-period quadratic Volterra kernel with antisymmetric coupling should yield <10% VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse echo error and <0.1% 100-period drift.
Train antisymmetric quadratic Volterra closures with 12-, 24-, and 36-period horizons; benchmark VP-Echo-OOD echo error and unforced 100-period drift.
VP-Echo-OOD three-pulse chirps: 24-period Volterra closure achieved 7.8% echo error and 0.05% unforced 100-period drift; 12-period error was 13.1%.
On VP-Echo-OOD 30-period pulse separations, 24-/36-period Volterra closures had 19.2%/14.3% echo error despite <0.1% energy drift.
Defer Volterra deployment: 24-period memory passes three-pulse chirps (7.8%) but even 36-period memory fails 30-period separations (14.3%).
Learn an adaptive multi-waterbag fluid closure with filament-preserving bag refinement and discrete-gradient field coupling for long-delay echoes.
Reconstruct waterbags from HermiteEcho-v1’s 64-moment outputs, train adaptive refinement, then benchmark held-out 30-period echoes and 100-period energy drift.
Initialize waterbags from HermiteEcho-v1’s 64-moment outputs; train adaptive refinement with discrete-gradient coupling; measure 30-period echo error and 100-period drift.
VP-Echo-OOD 30-period separations: adaptive waterbags achieved 8.9% echo error and 0.03% unforced 100-period drift versus Volterra’s 14.3%/0.09%.
Using HermiteEcho-v1’s 64-moment outputs, stress-test waterbag refinement on withheld chirped four-pulse histories, measuring echo error and unforced 100-period drift.
On withheld chirped four-pulse histories, adaptive waterbags had 16.2% echo error despite 0.04% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Publish WB-Chirp-OOD: withheld chirped four-pulse forcing histories, Vlasov–Poisson echo amplitudes, and 100-period energy-drift evaluation scripts.
Restrict adaptive waterbags to validated 30-period separations (8.9% echo error); defer general deployment after 16.2% error on chirped four-pulse histories.
Train a latent-characteristic closure that advects velocity-space phase markers and exchanges energy exactly with Poisson fields.
How many advected phase markers are needed to recover withheld four-pulse chirped echoes without compromising exact field-energy exchange?
Sixty-four adaptive velocity-phase markers should reduce WB-Chirp-OOD four-pulse echo error below 10% with <0.1% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Using WB-Chirp-OOD, train 32-, 64-, and 128-marker closures; measure four-pulse echo error and unforced 100-period energy drift.
WB-Chirp-OOD: 64 markers yielded 12.4% four-pulse echo error, exceeding 10%, despite 0.03% unforced 100-period energy drift.
Chirp-triggered redistribution of 128 phase markers should lower WB-Chirp-OOD four-pulse echo error below 10% while retaining <0.1% 100-period drift.
Implement chirp-triggered 128-marker redistribution; evaluate WB-Chirp-OOD four-pulse echo error and unforced 100-period energy drift.
WB-Chirp-OOD: redistributed 128 markers achieved 8.4% four-pulse echo error versus 64 markers’ 12.4%, with 0.04% unforced 100-period drift.
Release MarkerEcho-v1: chirp-triggered 128-marker redistribution, energy-exchange integrator, and WB-Chirp-OOD four-pulse evaluation scripts.
Adopt MarkerEcho-v1 for four-pulse chirps: redistributed 128 markers meet 8.4% echo error and 0.04% drift; 64 markers miss at 12.4%.
Use MarkerEcho-v1 for four-pulse chirps, HermiteEcho-v1 for three-pulse chirps, waterbags for 30-period separations; supersede EchoClosure-v1, defer Volterra.
